Small outfit, one job at a time

Prime Exteriors is run by Kurt out of Dallas in Melbourne’s north. The person who quotes your job is the person who turns up to do it, which is the whole reason this page is short on claims and long on things you can go and check for yourself.

  • Based in Dallas VIC 3047
  • 5.0 on Google from 37 reviews
  • 149 jobs through hipages since 2022
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. About

Who you are dealing with

One operator, working as a sole trader, doing exterior work only. Not a franchise, not a call centre that subcontracts your job to whoever is free, and not a general cleaning company that also does driveways.

That shape has a real upside and a real limit, and it is only fair to say both. The upside is that nothing gets lost between the quote and the work, and the person who looked at your render is the person choosing the chemistry for it. The limit is capacity: we are not the right call for a twenty building portfolio that needs forty crews on the same morning. For everything short of that, from a single driveway to a body corporate on a yearly cycle, it works.

Not claimed

Five things you will not find on this website

A team size

Because there is not one to quote. Exterior cleaning sites routinely say "our team of technicians" when it is one person and a trailer. If that changes here, this page changes with it.

An inflated history

The business was registered in December 2021 and that is what the page says. It is not dressed up as decades of family tradition.

Insurance and accreditation figures

Twenty million in public liability is the number every competitor prints. We are not printing a certificate number we have not shown you, so ask and it goes in writing with the quote.

Testimonials with no trail

The three testimonials on the old website could not be traced to any public source, so they are gone. Only reviews you can open and read yourself are used. The reviews.

Stock photography as our work

The old site used a stock photo of a model on a ladder. Photographs here are either a job we did, captioned as one, or a representative illustration that says so.

The actual trade

Exterior only, and that is on purpose

The outside of a building is a specialisation, not a sideline to interior cleaning. Narrowing to it is what makes it possible to know which chemistry belongs on a hundred year old bluestone plinth and which will ruin it.

What this business does

Cleaning, restoration and protection of outdoor surfaces.

  • Pressure and surface cleaning of driveways, paths, patios and hardstands
  • House and building washing, including render, cladding and soft washing
  • Windows, gutters, roof washing and solar panels
  • Stain and surface restoration: oil, rust, gum, efflorescence, paint and graffiti
  • Sealing and protective coatings for concrete, aggregate, paving and stone
  • Builders and handover cleaning on new residential and commercial work
  • Residential, commercial and body corporate property

What it does not

Work that belongs to another trade, and we will say so.

  • Interior cleaning, carpets, bond and end of lease work
  • Roof repairs, re-bedding, re-pointing and replacement
  • Gutter repair or replacement, as opposed to clearing and washing
  • Painting, rendering and any making good of a damaged surface
  • Landscaping, garden maintenance and rubbish removal
  • Anything above ground based reach without the right access engaged first

How the work is run

Three things that do not change job to job

The surface decides the method

Not the equipment that happens to be on the trailer. A render wall gets soft washed even when a pressure clean would be quicker, because pressure is what wrecks render.

A straight answer about outcomes

Some staining does not come out. An old oil patch in open aggregate improves substantially and does not vanish, and you will hear that before the job rather than after it.

A fixed price, in writing

Priced per surface from photos and measurements, not per hour. If something on site turns out to be worse than the photos showed, you get a call before any extra work happens, not an adjusted invoice afterwards.

What we do

Six service families covering the whole exterior of a property, from cleaning through to sealing.

Questions

Asked about the business itself

Is Prime Exteriors a one person business?

Yes, at the time of writing. Kurt quotes the work and does the work. For larger jobs that genuinely need two sets of hands, help is brought in, and you will be told that at quote stage rather than finding a stranger on your driveway.

We would rather say this plainly than print "our team" and hope nobody notices.

How long has the business been going?

Registered in December 2021, and trading through hipages since 2022 with 149 completed jobs on that profile. The Google profile is newer, which is why it carries fewer reviews at a higher rating.

There is no older trading history being quietly left out.

Are you insured?

Ask for the current certificate and it will come through with the quote. What we are not doing is printing a cover amount on a web page as a trust badge, because the number on its own tells you nothing and every competitor prints the same one.

For commercial and body corporate work, the certificate and the relevant documentation are provided before the first visit as a matter of course.

Do you subcontract the work out?

No. The job you book is the job we do. That is the main practical difference between this and booking through a platform that passes your address to whoever accepts it first.

What happens if something gets damaged?

You tell us, and it gets dealt with rather than argued about. The honest prevention is in the method: the reason render is soft washed and old tessellated tile is treated carefully is that those are the surfaces that do not recover from being cleaned wrong.

If a surface looks risky before we start, you will hear about it then, including when the answer is that we would rather not touch it.

Get A Quote

Send photos and you will get a real price

No site visit needed for most residential work. Photos, rough measurements and the suburb are enough to price almost anything.

  1. What you are looking atThe surface and what has gone wrong with it.
  2. A few photosWide enough to show the whole area, plus a close up of the worst part.
  3. A fixed pricePer surface and in writing, with anything we would not recommend spelled out.
